title: Kahana vs Facebook Groups: Living Room vs Library
excerpt: Facebook Groups is real-time chat, groups, and community velocity. Kahana is the shelf and reading list beside the chat, not another inbox.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: ≈1.8B people use Facebook Groups each month; 25M+ monthly active public groups.
Groups range from local communities and hobby/interest spaces to brand/customer communities and learning/education groups.
Built into Facebook’s main app and web; members’ names and pictures are visible, which can increase perceived trust.
Used heavily by brands and creators to grow business, promote eLearning, and generate leads as Page organic reach declines.

strengths.title: Direct line to audience, bypassing algorithms
strengths.detail: Groups provide a more direct channel to followers than public Page posts limited by feed algorithms.

strengths.title: High engagement and loyalty potential
strengths.detail: Engaged groups deepen relationships, encourage advocacy, and create intimate niche communities around brands or interests.

strengths.title: Versatile use cases (business, learning, community)
strengths.detail: Scale businesses, promote eLearning, collect feedback/feature requests, and run member-only content.

strengths.title: Built-in tools and moderation
strengths.detail: Admin tools (rules, moderation, membership controls), events, units/guides, and announcements structure group activity.

weaknesses.title: Dependent on Facebook’s ecosystem and policies
weaknesses.detail: UI, notifications, discovery, or moderation policy changes can impact reach and engagement.

weaknesses.title: Noise and quality management
weaknesses.detail: Large groups get noisy; need clear rules, moderators, and escalation paths for quality and safety.

weaknesses.title: Limited data portability and ownership
weaknesses.detail: Member data and content stay inside Facebook, less control than owning your own community platform.

weaknesses.title: Fighting the algorithm and distractions
weaknesses.detail: Group content can be buried; ads and unrelated Facebook noise compete for attention; notifications can overwhelm.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Facebook Groups is real-time chat, groups, and community velocity. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Spaces for people to connect with others who share their interests, free, familiar group communities inside Facebook.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Facebook Groups side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Facebook Groups you can use Memberships and Community & Messaging as first-class product jobs. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Facebook Groups

You can use both. Facebook Groups keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Facebook Groups. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
